Which do you think is better, iOS, or Android?

Better by which measure? I have a strong personal preference to Android OS, but that in no way indicates it's "better." In my opinion, for those wishing for a greater ability of customization and control over their mobile experience, Android is better suited. For those wishing for a simpler mobile experience, with less opportunity for things to "go wrong" (and the general restrictiveness that comes with it), iOS is better suited.

To better discuss which is better, you have to establish a value benchmark.

Android is better, but that is a personal preference. I can really make my phone "my phone" through Android by rooting, flashing a new rom, changing kernel rates and being able manipulate the CPU/GPU to run high quality games and watch high quality movies.

I like being able to have an app like ROM Toolbox that I can use to literally change every aspect of my phone, and I like being able to edit and change apps to perform to my specifications.

I agree with @OldSalt that iOS may be better for a simpler mobile experience, but when life is simple it isn't fun!

This is a very subjective question. iOS and Android both have their strengths and weaknesses.

For non tech savvy people, iOS is great. It's very stable and to the point. Idiot proof; very hard to mess up and brick unless you're modding it.

Android is better for power users as the possibilities are endless. However, unlike iOS Android is open for software modding so different phones can have different (slightly) interfaces. Moreover, with many different hardware manufacturers, there are many different hardware configurations.

Both have their merit. I'm a droid user and will admit my bias. However, I'd still rather my elderly mother have an iPhone.
